title: Minimum Sideway Jumps
summary: Given a 3-lane road of length n , a frog starts at point 0 in the second lane and aims to reach point n .
statement: Given a 3-lane road of length n , a frog starts at point 0 in the second lane and aims to reach point n . The road has obstacles at certain points, represented by an array of length n + 1 , where each element indicates an obstacle on a specific lane at a given point. If an element is 0, there is no obstacle at that point. The frog can jump to an adjacent lane or perform a side jump to a non-obstacle lane at the same point to avoid obstacles. The task is to determine the minimum number of side jumps needed for the frog to reach point n , starting from lane 2 at point 0. Note that there are no obstacles at points 0 and n .
constraints: The frog starts in lane two at point zero; endpoints contain no obstacle.
Forward moves cost zero and same-position lane changes cost one; return minimum side jumps.
hints: Track the cheapest cost to occupy each of the three lanes at the current point.
Block the obstacle lane before considering sideways changes.
For every open lane, keep its current cost or one plus the minimum open-lane cost.
Forward travel preserves cost, and every optimal side jump comes from the cheapest currently reachable open lane, so the three-state DP is complete.
editorial: Forward travel preserves cost, and every optimal side jump comes from the cheapest currently reachable open lane, so the three-state DP is complete.

tests.explanation: The frog must change lanes twice to pass the three staggered obstacles.
One early side jump reaches a lane that remains open.
